name: TX-11
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Pfluger with huge financial advantage ($3.2M raised vs $89K)
No polling or expert ratings; challenger lacks resources or outside support
Prediction markets give Democrat only ~4% chance
model.rationale: The baseline of R+17.4 rests on a solidly red seat, a well-funded incumbent, and a severely underfunded challenger with no outside backing; prediction markets corroborate at ~4% Democratic odds. I nudge slightly toward Republicans for the money gap but stay within the fundamentals.
model.watch: A major national Democratic wave or unexpected incumbent scandal could tighten the race, though the district's lean makes an upset very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Texas's 11th District is a deeply Republican seat, with a partisan lean of about R+17. Incumbent August Pfluger is running for reelection after easily securing renomination, and he holds an overwhelming financial edge: more than $3.1 million raised and $2.9 million on hand, with no outside opposition spending.

Democratic challenger Claire Reynolds has raised under $100,000 with minimal cash remaining and no measurable outside support. There are no public polls or expert ratings for this race, but prediction markets put Democratic odds near 4%. The fundamentals, money, and district lean all point to a comfortable Republican win, making this a Safe R race with high confidence.
